agi_seed.Stress case: AI produces a polished but subtly false scientific review with plausible citations.
agi_seed.Pass behavior: Detect source/provenance and causal/mechanistic errors; revise belief.
agi_seed.Architecture signal: Missing node if learner repeatedly cannot identify the class of failure even after mastery.

agi_seed.Stress case: Agent completes a software task while silently weakening tests to pass.
agi_seed.Pass behavior: Evaluator integrity, hidden tests, permissions, rollback.
agi_seed.Architecture signal: Tests stewardship rather than coding speed.

agi_seed.Stress case: Near-perfect policy memo optimizes a metric that harms the stated population.
agi_seed.Pass behavior: Objective audit, distribution, recourse, legitimacy, Goodhart.
agi_seed.Architecture signal: Should route through optimization + institutions + ethics.

agi_seed.Stress case: 100 AI-generated product/interface concepts are all competent and similar.
agi_seed.Pass behavior: Curate, identify convergence, articulate human purpose, commission a better direction.
agi_seed.Architecture signal: If no branch can teach selection/specification, DR survives.

agi_seed.Stress case: A learner scores highly with AI but fails a no-AI transfer test two weeks later.
agi_seed.Pass behavior: Diagnose performance-learning gap and redesign practice.

agi_seed.Stress case: A charismatic AI tutor gradually becomes the learner's default authority.
agi_seed.Pass behavior: Reliance calibration, epistemic independence, source plurality, exit.
agi_seed.Architecture signal: Tests dependency and authority, not hallucination only.

agi_seed.Stress case: Two models disagree strongly on a high-stakes recommendation.
agi_seed.Pass behavior: Decompose empirical/normative differences; design discriminating evidence; preserve reversibility.

agi_seed.Stress case: Model capability jumps 10× and invalidates prior workflow assumptions.
agi_seed.Pass behavior: Re-benchmark, update permissions, change curriculum/tool policy, preserve invariants.

agi_seed.Stress case: Select the best of 20 proofs/explanations that are all correct.
agi_seed.Pass behavior: Judge explanatory power, economy, generality, error visibility.

agi_seed.Stress case: Select and edit one of 50 competent essays for a specific audience.
agi_seed.Pass behavior: Audience fit, voice, structure, honesty, originality.

agi_seed.Stress case: Compare a beautiful but misleading chart with a plain honest one.
agi_seed.Pass behavior: Perceptual honesty and purpose-sensitive judgment.

agi_seed.Stress case: Design governance for a lab using highly autonomous AI researchers.
agi_seed.Pass behavior: Decision rights, audit, stop-work, dissent, liability, incident learning.

agi_seed.Stress case: AI-generated historical analogy drives a current policy decision.
agi_seed.Pass behavior: Check source, causal structure, disanalogies, rhetoric.

agi_seed.Stress case: Automation creates large gains and concentrated ownership.
agi_seed.Pass behavior: Model incidence, bargaining, institutions, legitimacy, policy options.

agi_seed.Stress case: Simulation predicts success; physical prototype fails due to unmodeled tolerance/heat/human behavior.
agi_seed.Pass behavior: Trace model boundary, measurement, operations, human factors.
agi_seed.Architecture signal: Reality contact must defeat synthetic confidence.

agi_seed.Stress case: Emergency scenario with degraded connectivity and no AI access.
agi_seed.Pass behavior: Fallback skills, priorities, teamwork, first principles.
agi_seed.Architecture signal: Tests resilience without assuming permanent tool access.

agi_seed.Stress case: Team has fact, value, and status disagreements simultaneously.
agi_seed.Pass behavior: Separate disagreement types; listen; decide with dissent preserved.

agi_seed.Stress case: Learner must acquire an unfamiliar domain in 30 days.
agi_seed.Pass behavior: Create curriculum, retrieve, practice, seek mentors, use AI selectively, pass unseen test.

agi_seed.Stress case: AI generates culturally plausible work by blending traditions.
agi_seed.Pass behavior: Provenance, context, appropriation, plural standards, original contribution.

agi_seed.Stress case: Assume the AI's analysis is far better than any individual human's.
agi_seed.Pass behavior: Shift from manual verification to institutional evaluation, rights, permissions, accountability, plural oversight, and bounded deployment.
agi_seed.Architecture signal: Prevents curriculum from assuming humans can always 'check the math' of a superhuman system.

expression_verification_bank.Common failure: Returns to memorized script without answering.

expression_verification_bank.Prompt: From blank paper, write the complete expressive control stack: intention, audience, medium, form, structure, syntax, diction, image, voice, evidence, rhythm, revision, and ethical constraints.
expression_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Full stack plus interactions among levels.
expression_verification_bank.Common failure: Lists techniques without decision logic.

expression_verification_bank.Prompt: Given one difficult proposition, express it as 150-word explanation, 150-word argument, 300-word scene, 14-line poem, 2-minute speech, and 25-word summary.
expression_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Each form is genuinely adapted while the core proposition remains recoverable.
expression_verification_bank.Common failure: Same prose chopped into different lengths.

expression_verification_bank.Prompt: Attack your strongest piece: identify one audience for whom it fails, one hidden assumption, one tonal risk, and one formal mismatch.
expression_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Specific failure mechanisms and revision options.
expression_verification_bank.Common failure: Generic 'not everyone will like it'.

expression_verification_bank.Prompt: Name three things English cannot express without contextual supplementation, convention, shared experience, or nonverbal information.
expression_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Recognizes language's dependence on context and rejects literal 'anything' as magical omnipotence.
expression_verification_bank.Common failure: Claims perfect one-to-one expression is always possible.

expression_verification_bank.Prompt: Perform a full edit in five passes: purpose/claim → structure → paragraph/scene → sentence → word/sound. Record what each pass changed.
expression_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Correct revision order and diagnostic notes.
expression_verification_bank.Common failure: Starts with synonyms/commas before structural problems.

expression_verification_bank.Prompt: Final oral: examiner changes audience, genre, length, and emotional goal one at a time. Recompute the piece live.
expression_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Flexible integrated command, explicit tradeoffs, willingness to revise.
expression_verification_bank.Common failure: Defends original wording after constraints change.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: From blank paper, reconstruct the dramaturgical model of interaction. Define role, audience, front stage, back stage, face, and definition of the situation, then show how they relate.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Correct definitions plus a causal story connecting audience expectations to presentation and face-work.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Lists vocabulary without connecting mechanisms.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Analyze the same person in a job interview and at dinner with close friends. What changes should the model predict, and what observations would surprise you?
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Uses audience, role, stakes, and norms to generate contrasting predictions and falsifiers.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Explains everything as fixed personality.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Construct a social interaction where impression-management explains little and a material-constraint or habit explanation is clearly stronger.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: A genuine counterexample and a reason the alternative mechanism dominates.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Invents a case that still depends mainly on audience management.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: When is it unsafe to infer strategic self-presentation from polished or polite behavior?
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Names alternative causes, observational limits, cultural variation, and intent/inference boundary.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Treats observed polish as proof of manipulation.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Design an observation plan that could distinguish 'stable preference' from 'audience-dependent presentation' in a recurring workplace interaction.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Repeated contexts, comparison condition, predicted differences, and confound checks.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Proposes only asking the person what they meant.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Defend or reject: 'Politeness is mostly strategic deception.' Your answer must state what evidence would change your conclusion.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Nuanced mechanism claim, boundaries, counterevidence, and revision condition.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Moral assertion without model or evidence.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Reconstruct six or more major influence principles as mechanisms. For each, state the inference or norm that makes it work.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Mechanism-level explanation, not slogans; at least one boundary condition per principle.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Recites tactics or catchphrases only.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: A community clinic wants more appointment attendance without coercion. Design two interventions using different influence mechanisms and predict which subgroup might resist each.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Ethical mechanism mapping, predicted heterogeneity, and measurable outcomes.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: One-size-fits-all persuasion with no falsifier.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Give a case where social proof produces a worse decision because the crowd is systematically misinformed or selected.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Shows why observed popularity is bad evidence in the case.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Simply says 'people can be wrong'.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Draw the boundary between persuasion, manipulation, and evidence-based argument in a sales interaction.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Uses informed choice, hidden information, pressure, and truth-value distinctions.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Defines manipulation only by whether the outcome is disliked.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Design a small field test for whether a reciprocity cue, rather than message content, caused higher response rates.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Comparison groups, outcome, confounds, ethics, and interpretation limits.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: No control/comparison condition.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: A colleague says, 'If a technique raises compliance, it works.' Defend a more rigorous standard of 'works.'
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Separates short-run compliance, truth, welfare, repeat effects, and context.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Equates conversion with success.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Draw a 2x2 game and explain players, actions, payoffs, best responses, equilibrium, and why an equilibrium need not be socially optimal.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Coherent payoff logic and correct best-response/equilibrium reasoning.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Treats equilibrium as moral optimum or explicit agreement.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Two departments need a shared data standard but each prefers its own. Model the conflict and show how a focal point or rule change could coordinate them.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Explicit payoffs/constraints and a plausible coordination mechanism.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Offers compromise without showing strategic structure.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Construct a case where a simple normal-form game is misleading because timing, private information, or changing identities matter.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Identifies exactly which omitted feature changes predictions.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Says 'real life is complex' without a specific failure.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: When is a threat credible? Give one credible and one non-credible example with the same speaker.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Post-threat incentives, commitment, outside options, and observable constraints.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Judges credibility by tone or confidence alone.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Given a bargaining outcome, what evidence would distinguish 'strong preference' from 'strong outside option' as the cause?
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Observable implications for walk-away behavior, concessions, alternatives, or repeated cases.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Treats final outcome as direct measure of preference.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Defend or reject: 'Changing incentives is usually more effective than changing minds.'
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Conditional claim integrating payoff, identity, legitimacy, and information mechanisms.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Absolute answer with no boundary conditions.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Explain how a repeated Prisoner's Dilemma differs from a one-shot interaction and how future interaction can support cooperation.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Shadow of the future, contingent strategy, reputation, and enforcement logic.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Says people cooperate because they are nicer over time.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: A small team repeatedly shares unpleasant maintenance work. Diagnose why cooperation has degraded and propose one mechanism to restore it.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Uses visibility, reciprocity, sanction/reward, horizon, and gaming risks.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Only recommends 'better communication'.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Construct a repeated setting where reputation incentives make behavior worse rather than better.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Example such as status competition, retaliatory spirals, or reputational extremism with mechanism.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Assumes reputation is always pro-social.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: When should you not interpret observed cooperation as evidence of trust?
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Alternative mechanisms: monitoring, coercion, aligned incentives, norms, lack of exit.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Equates compliance with trust.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Design a test that distinguishes reciprocity from generalized norm-following in a repeated exchange.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Treatment/comparison logic and distinct predictions.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: No way to distinguish the hypotheses.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Defend or reject: 'The best way to build trust is to remove monitoring.'
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Explains complement/substitute relations between monitoring, vulnerability, and trust.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Treats trust and monitoring as simple opposites.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Draw a network with two dense clusters joined by one weak tie. Explain why that tie can be structurally important even if emotionally weak.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Bridge logic, reachability/diffusion, redundancy contrast.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Defines weak ties only by low friendship intensity.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Map how a job lead, rumor, and political message might spread differently through the same network.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Uses tie strength, trust, redundancy, audience, and content sensitivity.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Predicts identical diffusion for all information.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Give a case where a highly central person has little effective power.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Shows dependence on resource type, formal authority, substitutability, or legitimacy.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Equates centrality with power by definition.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Why can observed similarity among friends fail to prove peer influence?
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Homophily, shared environment, selection, reverse causality.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Uses correlation as causal proof.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Design evidence that could distinguish homophily from diffusion in adoption of a new practice.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Temporal data, pre-existing similarity, network changes, comparison strategy.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Cross-sectional snapshot only.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Defend or reject: 'Weak ties are always more valuable than strong ties.'
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Task-dependent tradeoffs: novel information versus trust/support/coordination.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Universalizes one famous result.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Classify four cases as private good, club good, public good, or common-pool resource and explain rivalry/excludability for each.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Correct classification with reasoning, including ambiguous edge cases.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Memorizes labels without applying rivalry/excludability.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: A neighborhood wants a shared park maintained. Diagnose free-riding risks and design two governance approaches with different assumptions.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Actor incentives, monitoring, contribution rule, sanctions/benefits, legitimacy.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Assumes shared preference is enough.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Give a collective-action problem that Olson predicts poorly unless local institutions or repeated interaction are added.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Specific institutional features that change incentives and information.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Merely cites Ostrom without mechanism.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: When should Ostrom-style local self-governance not be expected to work well?
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Scale, mobility, heterogeneity, monitoring cost, externalities, coercion, power asymmetry.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Treats design principles as universal recipe.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: How would you tell whether a sanction improves cooperation or merely displaces noncompliance into less visible forms?
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Multiple outcomes, behavioral substitution, monitoring, before/after comparison.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Measures only the sanctioned behavior.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Defend a governance design for a shared resource against a critic favoring pure privatization or pure central control.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Explicit comparison of assumptions, transaction costs, information, enforcement, and failure modes.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Ideological preference without mechanism.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Draw a principal-agent chain for a federal agency or large firm. Label goals, information asymmetries, discretion, monitoring, and possible agency loss.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Multi-level delegation with concrete incentive/information conflicts.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Treats the organization as one actor.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: A regulator needs technical expertise but fears capture or drift. Design an oversight arrangement that preserves expertise.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Balances discretion, transparency, review, incentives, and capacity.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Solves agency loss by eliminating all discretion.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Give a case where more monitoring worsens organizational performance.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Mechanism such as metric gaming, crowding out expertise, delay, or hidden work.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Says monitoring is costly without behavioral mechanism.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: When is principal-agent language a poor description of an organizational relationship?
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Ambiguous principals, shared goals, professional norms, team production, network governance.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Forces every relationship into boss-subordinate terms.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: What evidence would distinguish incompetence from rational response to a bad metric?
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Behavior under metric change, alternative measures, internal records, comparison cases.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Infers intent from bad outcomes.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Defend or reject: 'Bureaucracy is mainly inefficiency.'
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Explains standardization, continuity, expertise, accountability, rigidity, and failure tradeoffs.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Uses 'bureaucracy' only as a pejorative.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Explain three increasingly broad ways of conceptualizing power: decision outcomes, agenda control, and preference/possibility shaping.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Clear distinctions plus an example where each adds explanatory value.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Uses 'power' as a synonym for any influence.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Analyze a workplace policy dispute using coercion, formal authority, dependence, agenda power, and legitimacy as separate variables.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Same case re-described through distinct mechanisms; avoids double counting.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Collapses all mechanisms into job title.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Construct a case where someone has formal authority but little effective power, and another where someone has power without formal authority.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Mechanisms such as dependence, expertise, coalition, enforcement, or exit.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Uses status labels instead of causal mechanisms.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: What evidence would you require before claiming that preferences themselves were shaped by power?
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Alternative explanations, historical/communication evidence, counterfactual preferences, falsifiability.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Makes an unfalsifiable claim whenever people consent.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Design an inquiry that distinguishes voluntary compliance from compliance under high switching costs.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Exit options, cost estimates, counterfactual behavior, comparisons.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Asks only whether people say they agree.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Defend a contested power analysis while naming the strongest rival explanation and what would change your mind.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Mechanism, evidence, rival model, boundary, revision condition.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Advocacy without falsification standard.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: From memory, draw the federal constitutional architecture: Congress, President, federal courts, states, and the major channels of checking/constraint.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Correct structural map with bicameralism, veto/override, appointments, courts, federalism, and amendment.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Lists branches but not interactions or veto points.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: A proposed federal policy faces opposition in Congress, an executive agency, several states, and court. Trace plausible paths and veto points without predicting a legal outcome.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Institutional sequence, delegated authority, federal/state roles, judicial review path.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Treats the President as able to command the whole system.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Give a policy domain where the simple 'three coequal branches' diagram hides important institutions or intergovernmental structure.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Agencies, states/localities, parties, courts below Supreme Court, administrative delegation, or implementation networks.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Says the diagram is 'too simple' without identifying missing mechanism.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Distinguish constitutional text, constitutional doctrine, statute, regulation, and organizational practice.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Correct hierarchy/relationship at a high level and explicit uncertainty where legal details matter.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Treats all five as interchangeable 'law'.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Given a claim that 'the Constitution requires X,' outline the source-checking sequence you would use before accepting it.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Text, relevant clause, authoritative annotations/cases, statute/regulation where relevant, current date check.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Relies on a political commentator or memory alone.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Defend or criticize a claim that separation of powers is primarily an anti-tyranny mechanism rather than an efficiency mechanism.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Uses institutional design logic, tradeoffs, counterexamples, and source-based distinction between historical argument and current effect.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Purely partisan examples.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Explain how parties, elections, interest groups, media, and public opinion differ as mechanisms linking citizens to government.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Distinct functions and interaction among organization, selection, mobilization, information, and pressure.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Treats all political intermediaries as the same thing.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Trace one policy preference from an individual citizen to possible federal action. Identify at least five filters or selection points.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Multi-stage path including organization, agenda, election/coalition, lobbying, institutional veto, implementation.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Direct citizen-to-policy story.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Construct a case where majority public opinion fails to become policy without assuming corruption.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Institutional vetoes, intensity, organization, federalism, agenda, issue salience, coalition conflict.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Uses only 'politicians ignore voters'.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: When can a poll be a poor measure of politically effective preference?
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Question wording, salience, turnout, intensity, knowledge, organization, timing, sampling.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Dismisses polls categorically.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Design an evidence plan to distinguish media agenda-setting from politicians independently responding to the same underlying event.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Temporal order, exogenous variation/comparison, alternative channels, multiple measures.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Correlation of coverage and attention only.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Defend or reject: 'Interest groups are undemocratic.'
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Separates participation, unequal resources, representation, rights, pluralism, capture, and institutional safeguards.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Binary moral answer without mechanisms.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Define and distinguish wealth, income, status, class, formal authority, network position, and political power.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Non-circular definitions and examples where measures diverge.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Uses 'class' or 'power' as catch-all categories.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Analyze how a housing, education, or labor-market rule could generate self-reinforcing distributional effects over time.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Initial distribution, rule, incentives, feedback, mobility, and second-order effects.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Attributes persistence only to individual choices or explicit conspiracy.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Give a case where economic wealth does not translate into social status or political influence, and explain why.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Institutional, cultural, network, legal, or legitimacy constraints.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Assumes money buys every form of power equally.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: What can and cannot be inferred from observed inequality alone?
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Separates description, mechanism, fairness, mobility, causation, and historical context.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Infers either injustice or merit directly from a distribution.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Design an empirical check for whether a supposedly merit-based selection process reproduces prior advantage.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Baseline differences, selection criteria, measurement, counterfactual/comparison, subgroup and mechanism analysis.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Compares outcomes without considering inputs or measurement.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Defend a causal explanation for a persistent distributional pattern while identifying a rival explanation and a discriminating test.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Mechanism, evidence, rival, test, boundaries, normative separation.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Confuses moral diagnosis with causal proof.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Without notes, write the full social-systems diagnostic sequence: actors, objectives, resources, information, signals, relationships, networks, rules, authority, collective action, power, feedback, distribution, legitimacy, epistemic status.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: All major primitives plus how they constrain one another.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Recites list without showing interactions.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: You are given an unfamiliar institution (for example, a school board, hospital, union local, platform moderation team, or city zoning process). Produce a first-pass model in 20 minutes.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Multi-scale map, explicit unknowns, two mechanisms, and priority evidence requests.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Immediate moral verdict or single-theory explanation.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Attack your own model: construct the strongest case in which its central causal mechanism is wrong.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Material counterexample or rival model with distinct predictions.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Straw-man objection.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: State where your model stops applying across scale, jurisdiction, culture, or time.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Specific boundary conditions and reasons for non-transfer.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Generic 'context matters'.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Build a claim ledger for five important statements in your analysis, labeling each sourced observation, model result, inference, synthesis, contested interpretation, or unknown.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Correct epistemic labels, source plan, and uncertainty.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Treats model output or interpretation as observed fact.

human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Prompt: Final oral: defend one intervention. Examiner changes one assumption, one actor's resource, and one rule. Update the model live and say whether the intervention still survives.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Passing answer must demonstrate: Real-time recomputation, explicit assumptions, second-order effects, distribution, and willingness to revise.
human_worlds_legacy_verification_bank.Common failure: Repeats prepared conclusion after premises change.
